open_obligations: Verify the 'over 90%' judge-agreement figure against Khan et al.'s reported consultant win rates
Check Khan et al.'s Elo-accuracy results for GPT-4-level debaters to see whether the trend is ambiguous there
Compare with Arnesen et al.'s own measurement that an untrained GPT-4-Turbo judge agreed with the consultant 72% of the time (p4 L47-49)
out.other_title: More persuasive consultants lower judge accuracy; optimisation favours incorrect side
out.rationale: The authors point to a limitation of Khan et al.'s evaluation (a sycophantic judge favouring consultants, and an ambiguous trend at GPT-4 level) rather than reporting a conflicting rerun, so CRITIQUES fits. Their response in this paper is to fine-tune a calibrated judge (Section 3.1).
out.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Whether consultancy baselines judged by a prompted GPT-4T are a fair comparison for debate; concerns Khan et al.'s consultancy optimization results

text: The authors acknowledge that Khan et al. (2024) found debate beats a single-consultancy-like baseline, with the effect growing with debater ability. They argue, however, that the skill-accuracy relationship is ambiguous for GPT-4-level models and that Khan et al.'s consultancy results optimize against a GPT-4T judge that is overly sycophantic, agreeing with their strongest consultants over 90% of the time.
title: Arnesen et al. argue Khan et al.'s consultancy results rest on an overly sycophantic GPT-4T judge
